assumptions.claim: The DMA transfer width register (driven from control registers) must never take the value 2'b11, as it is not defined in dma_transfer_width_e.
assumptions.risk: Undefined transfer width may cause incorrect data packing/striding, leading to data corruption or read/write beyond intended bounds.

assumptions.claim: The opcode register must never carry values other than 4'h0-4'h3 (OpcCopy, OpcSha256, OpcSha384, OpcSha512); all other 4-bit patterns are undefined.
assumptions.risk: Executing an undefined opcode could start an unintended operation, possibly accessing memory or exposing digest state.

assumptions.claim: The DMA control state register must stay within the enumerated states (0-10); values 11-15 are not defined and must not occur.
assumptions.cond: always while DMA FSM is active
assumptions.risk: Landing in an undefined state could cause protocol deadlock, invalid memory transactions, or security checks to be bypassed.

assumptions.claim: The DMA error type register must only carry values corresponding to the defined dma_error_e members (0-8); codes 9-31 are undefined.
assumptions.risk: An undefined error code could be misrouted, mask real errors, or trigger erroneous fatal/lifecycle escalation.

assumptions.claim: The ASID register must only carry the three defined encodings (OtInternalAddr=4'h7, SocControlAddr=4'ha, SocSystemAddr=4'h9); any other 4-bit value violates the FI-protected encoding scheme.
assumptions.cond: always when ASID is used for address-space access decisions
assumptions.risk: A malicious or faulty ASID value could bypass address-space separation, granting unauthorized access to internal, control, or system memory regions.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment claims ASID uses a 4-bit FI protected encoding with minimum Hamming distance of 2 bits, but no assertion or check ensures the three defined encodings (7, a, 9) actually satisfy this property, and no mechanism prevents future additions from violating it.
uncertain_points.cond: always when ASID encodings are interpreted
uncertain_points.risk: If the Hamming distance is insufficient, a single-bit fault injection could flip one valid encoding into another, bypassing access control and allowing illegal memory accesses.
